title: The Local AI Stack — Data API v1 (AI Rigs hardware)
description: Formal JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for the 'Show Off Your AI Rig' thread dataset published at /data/api/v1/hardware.json (and the unversioned copy at /data/hardware.json). Two-pass parse: pass 1 keyword-matches relevant posts; pass 2 extracts structured fields from the post's own text (quoted content excluded — a reply quoting someone else's rig does not credit the replying user). Extraction is conservative: a field the post does not state is null, never guessed (a 'jealous of the MI210' envy line and an 'I might get a couple of DGX sparks' hypothetical are not specs). A post describing several machines (multiple neofetch blocks) yields one record per machine. Every item keeps a 300-char preview as the fallback. See /data/api/README.md for the full contract and changelog.

version.description: Data API version (major.minor). Present on the published /data/api/v1/ copy; absent on the repo-root /data/hardware.json copy.

source.description: Display name of the source thread.

count.description: Number of records in 'items'. Must equal len(items).

items.description: One record per rig (a post with multiple machines contributes one record each).

id.description: Stable unique identifier: rigs_post_<post-number>_<n>, where <n> indexes the machine within a multi-machine post.

post_id.description: The Discourse post id (for deep links to the source post).

post_number.description: The post's number within the thread.

contributor.description: The forum username of the post's author.

gpu.description: The machine's primary GPU. Neofetch 'GPU n:' lines are grouped by model and the dominant one wins (a baseboard iGPU does not outvote eight A4000s); otherwise count phrases ('4x 9700 pro', 'a pair of R9700s', 'Dual 5060ti') and 'GPU:' label lines. Vendor words are only carried when the post states them.

model.description: GPU model as stated (e.g. 'NVIDIA RTX A4000', 'AMD Instinct MI210', 'R9700', 'M4 Max'). null when the post does not state one the poster owns.

count.description: Number of that GPU (1 when unstated). null when no model is known.

vram_total_gb.description: Total VRAM in GB, from figures the post states: an explicit total ('Total 40GB'), per-card capacity next to the GPU model multiplied by the stated count ('Dual 5060ti 16g' -> 32), or unified memory ('128GB M4 Max'). null when not stated — per-card sizes are never filled in from outside knowledge.

cpu.description: CPU as stated (neofetch 'CPU:' lines cleaned of (R) marks, thread counts, and clocks; 'CPU:' label lines; bare model mentions in a first-person statement). null when not stated.

ram_gb.description: System RAM in GB as stated ('128GB DDR4', '64 gig ddr4', neofetch 'Memory: x / y GiB' total). null when not stated.

storage.description: Storage as stated, joined with ' + ' when there are several drives (e.g. '2x 4TB Samsung NVMe + 6x 2TB Samsung 870 EVO'). Vague mentions ('Some storage', 'Storage: Yes') are not quantified and stay null.

os.description: Operating system as stated (neofetch 'OS:' line, or Ubuntu / Debian / Fedora / Arch / EndeavourOS / Windows / macOS / Proxmox / Rocky / AlmaLinux). null when not stated.

workload.description: What the machine runs: model + backend + context + verbatim speed snippets ('Qwen 3.8 27B FP8 via vllm-radiance | Roughly 3200t/s prefill, 80t/s general generation, 120t/s code gen'). null when the post reports no workload.

notes.description: Secondary signals: spare GPUs, power draw ('150W idle / 400W under load'), PSU size. Joined with ' | '. null when none found.

preview.description: The first 300 chars of the post text — always present, the fallback for posts where structured extraction found nothing.

structured.description: true when at least one hardware field (gpu / vram_total_gb / cpu / ram_gb / storage / os) was extracted; false for preview-only items.
